requirements.statement: Projects Hub has one central Mira Live agent as the sole semantic orchestrator of the conversation; transport and product tools do not introduce a second hidden ASR/LLM router or deterministic semantic brain.
acceptance: Online speech reaches the configured Live model as audio in the same conversational session.
Offline saved speech is deliberately replayed to that same central Live agent rather than summarized or transcribed by a second semantic pipeline.
Deterministic code is limited to transport, authentication, bounded orchestration, schemas, persistence, idempotency, telemetry, mechanical formatting and fail-closed checks.

An explicit owner-authorized note-structuring capability may call Gemini on already accepted, Mira-selected text and server-derived authorship/roles. It is not a hidden pre-Live summarizer, second ASR or conversation router.

requirements.statement: The primary online voice transport is authenticated same-origin WSS between the Projects Hub client and Projects Hub backend, which alone talks to the Live provider; once a session attaches WSS it never silently falls back to HTTP audio input.
acceptance: Bootstrap returns a same-origin socket URL, one-use short-lived ticket, attempt identifier and versioned protocol.
Tickets are transported only through the WebSocket subprotocol and are rejected when stale, reused, cross-resource, query-carried or foreign-origin.
PCM uses bounded binary frames with relay ACK/backpressure; model events and audio are pushed over the socket.
A transport gap during an open speech turn cannot execute a mutation until a later clean turn is admitted.

requirements.statement: Several people may use Projects Hub concurrently with isolated private conversations, Live sessions and tool permissions. Explicitly shared project objects/results are accessible only through current project grants; every session and tool call remains bound to the authenticated issuer subject, workspace and conversation, with explicit bounded capacity.
acceptance: Conversation resource bindings include workspace, authenticated subject and conversation identity.
A user cannot renew, attach to, read events from, stop or mutate another user's Live session by guessing identifiers.
Global Live concurrency is bounded and configurable; overload fails visibly instead of creating unbounded queues or cross-session degradation.
Capacity and authorization remain correct under concurrent session starts.
Publishing a project note, discussion entry, question or analysis shares only that authorized object; it never opens the author's full private transcript/source or unrelated project data.

requirements.statement: Voice capture and replay are loss-aware: accepted/durable source state is explicit, stale unacknowledged transport audio is not replayed after a gap, and reconnect/retry cannot duplicate an accepted semantic mutation.
acceptance: Offline audio is durably stored on-device before deliberate replay and is deleted only after confirmed server disposition.
WSS reconnect uses a fresh ticket/generation and does not replay expired pending PCM.
Mutating tools remain idempotent and success is claimed only after authoritative receipt/readback.

requirements.statement: Projects Hub participates in the common product-family OAuth/OIDC identity plane using stable issuer+subject identity while preserving separate resource audiences, ACLs and delegated grants for every connected project.
acceptance: A token minted for Projects Hub is never forwarded to Regional Knowledge, Street Story or another protected resource.
Cross-project access obtains a resource-specific user-authorized token/grant and every target service re-authorizes the subject.
No global service-role impersonation is used for normal user actions.

requirements.statement: Mira can use the user's authorized Regional Knowledge Base as a read capability inside the same Projects Hub conversation, through a narrow evidence-returning knowledge search interface rather than a second conversational agent.
acceptance: The Live tool surface exposes Regional Knowledge progressively and keeps the active capability bundle small.
Knowledge results preserve exact evidence/provenance references and inherited access controls.
Regional Knowledge unavailability is surfaced without breaking unrelated Projects Hub conversation capabilities.

requirements.statement: Cross-project POI integration has one ownership model: Regional Knowledge owns source/book evidence, Street Story owns the canonical regional POI identity/claims/contradiction state, and Projects Hub acts as an authorized expert-review/work surface without duplicating those authoritative stores.
acceptance: Ambiguous POI identity creates an unresolved review path rather than a silent duplicate or merge.
Expert decisions are written back to the owning service and are considered saved only after receipt/readback.
Projects Hub does not create a parallel canonical fact or contradiction database.

requirements.statement: After the first Android installation, normal product updates are discoverable from inside the app: the user is notified that a signed release is available and can start download/verification/system installation with a simple update action instead of reacquiring the APK from source.
acceptance: The app checks the public release manifest on launch/resume and exposes a visible update action when versionCode increases.
Downloaded APK bytes are SHA-256 verified and Android's package installer/signature protections remain in the path.
Update failure leaves the currently installed app usable and retryable.

requirements.statement: Critical Projects Hub requirements are a protected development contract: implementation may evolve, but a tool or agent must not silently weaken or reinterpret a critical requirement without an explicit owner requirement-change instruction.
acceptance: DevCoveer exposes this requirements manifest automatically to implementation/review tasks.
Changes that conflict with a critical statement are surfaced as a conflict rather than normalized into a new requirement.
An intentional requirement change uses the requirements-update path with an explicit authorization reference.

requirements.statement: Mira may control light/dark theme by voice and provides incremental adaptive onboarding based on capabilities the user has not recently used, without dumping a long feature list or bloating the default Live tool surface.
acceptance: Theme control is a small deterministic UI capability.
Onboarding offers one or a few relevant tips and can stop when the user declines.
Onboarding state is product metadata, not a second semantic agent.

requirements.statement: The product family has one first-party stable user identity and authorization plane shared by mobile apps, web apps and MCP clients; external identity providers are optional authentication methods rather than the canonical user identity, and access to applications, services and Projects Hub projects is granted explicitly.
acceptance: One stable first-party subject identifies the same person across product-family applications and MCP resources.
A newly authenticated person receives no implicit platform-owner role, all-application access or all-project access.
The unique platform owner is explicitly bound to a stable first-party subject and is never inferred from email, display name or external-provider account.
Application/MCP resource grants have explicit audiences/scopes and can be revoked independently.
Projects Hub maintains explicit workspace/project memberships and lists only projects granted to the current actor.

Android authentication does not depend on an embedded WebView sharing cookies with an external provider; first-party passkey/invite authentication is the preferred target and external IdPs remain optional linked methods.
Street Story authentication is not migrated until its current functional acceptance is complete.

requirements.statement: Only the explicit platform owner may use Projects Hub to turn conversation-discovered product gaps into a durable development backlog and explicitly launch bounded implementation batches through the existing GitHub/DevCoveer delivery path; ordinary users have no development fallback.
acceptance: Mira can create/refine typed development requests containing the observed gap, desired outcome, relevant project/repository, acceptance criteria and evidence/context.
Development requests are durable, reviewable and batchable; conversation alone never authorizes implementation.
Starting implementation requires an explicit current owner command and produces durable batch status, tests/CI and deployment/readback evidence.
Owner-only development tools are absent from ordinary users' Live tool surfaces and direct API calls are independently authorization-checked.
Android changes delivered through self-development end in the normal signed release/update-manifest path so installed apps can self-update.

A sufficient owner answer may resume an already explicitly authorized execution within its existing scope exactly once; a question, note, recommendation or answer alone does not authorize a new implementation goal. PR #87 remains owner-paused until a separate implementation instruction.

requirements.statement: Project boards are voice-first and LLM-first: the user does not manually create, edit, drag, resize or type into board objects. Board mutations are performed only by the central Mira Live agent interpreting user speech and calling board tools. The board UI is primarily a read-only visual surface with camera/focus controlled via voice or minimal view controls.
acceptance: There is no primary user-facing text editor, drag-to-move, or toolbar for creating/editing stickies in the normal product path.
Board write tools are exposed to Mira (execution_origin=mira) and require authenticated Live session plus project editor rights.
Opening or closing the board does not break the ongoing voice session, microphone, transcript, or next turn admission.
Mira receives structural viewport/context (visible object ids, short texts, focus state) rather than relying on screenshots as the primary understanding path.
Guest share remains view-only; guests cannot mutate the board.

requirements.statement: Strong-model project analysis is an explicit, provided-context-only capability separate from owner self-development: it uses frozen authorized note, document, task, discussion or board evidence with consult_model/council_run, context_mode=provided_only, evidence_bundle and request_key, and cannot start development write tasks.
acceptance: Analytics client allowlist excludes start_task and other development write tools.

Analysis input is a frozen snapshot of selected authorized note, document, task, discussion or board source references/revisions plus an explicit question; no arbitrary project filesystem read for ordinary analysis.
Idempotent dispatch uses request_key; uncertain dispatch is represented as dispatch_unknown rather than blind retry.
Analysis results may be published back to the board as document cards; this does not grant development write access.

Analysis of an authorized note/document/task does not require board objects. Shared results use explicit project audiences, and typed addressed questions connect to the common answer/continuation path.

requirements.statement: Each user has one active personal conversation timeline across discussed projects; project focus and provider sessions do not create separate project chats or canvases.
acceptance: Durable message and turn IDs preserve text, voice references and typed widget blocks through reload/reconnect and late canonical transcription.
Shared project artifacts do not make the personal timeline readable by colleagues.

requirements.statement: Functional widget blocks are part of Mira's messages in the personal timeline; each project has one canonical board and the client mounts at most one board viewport, including optional expanded mode.
acceptance: Notes, questions, tasks and analysis expose useful content/actions inline; popup windows alone do not satisfy the requirement.
Switching/closing a board releases the prior renderer, large scene resources and subscriptions; historical board messages remain lightweight references.
Board content mutations remain Mira-only typed tools; pan/zoom/focus and explicit predefined actions are allowed without introducing a general text composer.

requirements.statement: Basic project collaboration includes a durable shared note with repository Markdown, server-derived author identity and role list, in-app reading/listening/discussion and explicit project audience.
acceptance: A clear save-note command uses already accepted text, explicit Gemini structuring and a configured project repository write with receipt/readback; retries do not duplicate notes or files.
Reuse the existing my-data-hub text-summary schema/prompt/renderer through a narrow versioned capability/adaptation, without fake audio or a second transcription pipeline.
A second authorized participant can read in the app without a personal GitHub account and publish a related authored reply; full private conversation and source audio remain private.
Model-suggested tasks/decisions are labelled as proposals until an authorized user actually adopts them; author role snapshots do not grant permissions.

Repository visibility and access must match the configured note audience; a project-restricted note cannot be written to a public repository under the false protection of app ACL. Public notes require an explicitly public project binding.

requirements.statement: Questions are durable addressed collaboration objects shared by notes, discussion, tasks, readiness, analysis and owner-development; Mira uses common context naturally and supports individual or grouped answers.
acceptance: Questions bind current authorized recipients, source revisions, blocking/nonblocking dependencies and expected continuations; multiple roles per member are supported.
One utterance can answer several unambiguous questions; unknown, skip and defer are distinct valid outcomes and do not fabricate approval.
Viewing, swiping, notification delivery, noise and damaged turns do not constitute an answer; accepted typed answers are versioned and idempotent.
Sufficient partial answers allow unrelated nonblocking work to proceed while unresolved required dependencies remain visible.

requirements.statement: Accepted collaboration work and authorized question continuations progress on a bounded durable server worker independent of an open client or Live session; reading status never advances execution.
acceptance: Answer receipt and continuation intent are persisted together; lease/retry/restart and external readback prevent duplicate semantic effects.

A real note/analysis/task continuation and an explicitly authorized owner needs_owner continuation resume correctly after client close and service restart; acceptance may use a pre-existing execution or a reproducibly prepared bounded execution within the launched implementation.
Use the existing durable store and a small bounded queue/pump; no generic workflow engine or new broker is required for the prototype.
Owner-only development permissions and existing design/review/delivery gates remain enforced for every continuation.

requirements.statement: On generic opening communication Mira starts with important information addressed personally to the user; general project activity is offered afterward as an optional summary, and a concrete user request takes priority.
acceptance: App launch displays a quiet personal brief without unsolicited speech; a generic greeting may speak the personal priorities.
General activity can summarize authored changes with source links only after opt-in; declining or deferring does not trigger repeated offers on every reconnect.
Seen, answered and deferred states remain distinct; only authorized project information appears in the user's brief.
